Cash-Book: Smart Finance & Digital Ledger

Declaration

We hereby declare that the project "Cash-Book: Smart Finance & Digital Ledger" is our original work completed as part of our academic requirements. The project provides an online platform for personal and small business finance management, featuring tracking of daily transactions, party ledgers, EMI/subscriptions, receipt management, and deep analytics.

Cash-Book is developed using React, Node.js, and MongoDB, representing a complete, full-stack, scalable digital ledger solution.

We sincerely thank our guide and our parents and family members for their continuous support, guidance, and encouragement throughout this project.

We further declare that this work has not been submitted to any other institution for any degree, diploma, or certificate.

Cash-Book: Smart Finance & Digital Ledger
1. Introduction of Project
  • It aims to simplify personal and small business finance management by offering a fast, convenient, and accessible way to track income, expenses, and debts.
  • The platform eliminates the limitations of traditional paper ledgers, such as data loss, manual calculation errors, and restricted physical access.
  • It offers essential financial management features including:
    • User registration & secure authentication
    • Daily transaction tracking (Income/Expense) categorized dynamically
    • Party Ledger (Udhaar Book) for tracking debts and credits
    • EMI & Subscription tracking with calendar views
    • Receipts Vault for securely storing bill images
    • Advanced analytics and summary reports
    • Shared cashbooks through user invitations
  • For admins, the system includes:
    • System analytics and user metrics
    • Transaction and cashbook oversight
    • Platform setting configurations
  • Cash-Book acts as a digital companion, allowing users to make informed financial decisions through clear insights and organized records.
  • The project uses modern web technologies:
    • Frontend: React (Vite)
    • Backend: Node.js (Express)
    • Database: MongoDB (Mongoose)
  • It serves as a real-world implementation of an end-to-end financial SaaS solution.

3. Technology Study
❖ React :
  • React was first developed by Jordan Walke at Facebook in 2011.
  • React is a JavaScript library used for building user interfaces (UI), especially single-page applications (SPA).
  • React uses a component-based architecture, where the UI is divided into reusable pieces called components.
  • React uses a Virtual DOM to efficiently update only the parts of the page that change, improving performance.
  • Vite is used as the build tool, providing a faster and leaner development experience for modern web projects.
❖ HTML & Tailwind CSS :
  • First developed by Tim Berners-Lee in 1990, HTML is short for Hypertext Markup Language.
  • HTML is used to create electronic documents (called pages) that are displayed on the World Wide Web.
  • Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework used in this project to rapidly build custom user interfaces without leaving the HTML/JSX.
❖ JavaScript :
  • JavaScript is a dynamic computer programming language.
  • It is lightweight and most commonly used as a part of web pages.
  • JavaScript allows client-side scripts to interact with the user and fetch dynamic data asynchronously.
❖ Node.js & Express.js :
  • Node.js was developed by Ryan Dahl in 2009.
  • It allows running JavaScript outside the browser (on the server side), using the V8 JavaScript engine.
  • Express.js is a minimal and flexible Node.js web application framework that provides a robust set of features for web and mobile applications.
  • It is used in this project to create RESTful APIs to handle frontend requests securely.
6
Cash-Book: Smart Finance & Digital Ledger
❖ MongoDB :
  • MongoDB was first released in 2009 by MongoDB Inc.
  • MongoDB is an open-source NoSQL database.
  • It stores data in flexible, JSON-like documents instead of tables, making it perfect for dynamic data models.
  • MongoDB is schema-less by nature, though Mongoose is used in this project to enforce structured schemas.
  • It is designed for high performance, scalability, and flexibility.
❖ Development Tools:
  • VS Code (Visual Studio Code): A free, open-source code editor developed by Microsoft. It is widely used for coding, debugging, and software development.
  • Postman: Used for API testing and endpoint verification.
  • Git & GitHub: Used for version control and source code management.

Cash-Book: Smart Finance & Digital Ledger
4. Objectives
  • The objective of the project Cash-Book is to design and develop a professional, responsive, and user-friendly web application for personal and small-business finance tracking.
  • The platform offers essential features such as transaction logging, categorization, receipt attachments, party ledger for debts/credits, and subscription tracking.
  • The aim is to deliver a scalable system that helps users gain complete control and visibility over their financial flow.

Start To End Process

1. Project Planning & Requirement Analysis
  • Define the purpose of the website: digital ledger and financial management.
  • Identify key features for users: transaction management, dynamic categories, invitations (shared cashbooks), and analytics.
  • Finalize the technology stack: React, Tailwind CSS (frontend), Node.js, Express, and MongoDB (backend).
2. UI/UX Design
  • Design a modern, clean, and responsive dashboard interface.
  • Use intuitive color schemes (green for income, red for expense) and high-quality icons.
  • Incorporate animations (Framer Motion) to enhance user experience.
3. Frontend Development
  • Use React for building the frontend user interface.
  • Build pages such as: Dashboard Home, Transactions, Party Ledger, Receipts Vault, EMI Tracker, and Settings.
8
Cash-Book: Smart Finance & Digital Ledger
4. Backend Development
  • Use Node.js with Express.js to handle user authentication, transaction logic, and data aggregation.
  • Connect to MongoDB via Mongoose for managing backend data like:
    • Users
    • Transactions and Cashbooks
    • Categories and Payment Modes
    • Invitations and Receipts
  • Implement secure authentication (JWT) for API protection.
5. Functionality Implementation
  • User Side: Registration/Login, add/edit/delete transactions, filter by date/category, manage debts, view graphical reports.
  • Admin Side: System analytics, manage all users, oversee total transactions across the platform.
6. Testing & Optimization
  • Perform end-to-end testing of form validations, API response times, and state management.
  • Optimize UI rendering using React hooks and lazy loading components.

8. Database Design
❖ Collection Name: User
Field Name Data Type Constraints Description
username String Required, Trimmed User's display name
email_id String Required, Unique User's email (Primary key identifier)
password String Required Hashed password
mobile String Required Contact number
role String Enum: [0, 1] 0 = Admin, 1 = User
❖ Collection Name: Transaction
Field Name Data Type Constraints Description
title String Required Title of transaction
type String Required (income/expense) Transaction type
amount Number Required Transaction value
date String Required Date (YYYY-MM-DD)
chalan_id String Required Links to a Cashbook
category String Default: '' Transaction category
user_email String Required Email of the user who made it
party_type String Enum: [creditor, debtor] For party ledger entries
❖ Collection Name: Cashbook
Field Name Data Type Constraints Description
chalan_id String Required, Unique Unique ID of the cashbook
chalan_name String Required Display name of cashbook
user_email String Required Owner's email
13
Cash-Book: Smart Finance & Digital Ledger
❖ Collection Name: Invitation
Field Name Data Type Constraints Description
invite_name String Required Name of the invitee
invite_email String Required Email of the invited user
inviter_email String Required Email of the user sending invite
cashbook_id String Required The cashbook being shared
status String Enum: [pending, accepted, rejected] Current status of invite
❖ Collection Name: Receipt
Field Name Data Type Constraints Description
title String Required Description of the receipt
file_url String Required URL/Base64 of the receipt image
user_email String Required Owner's email
date String Required Date of upload
